name: query
summary: Compiles a structured, JSON-serializable Spec into a runnable query for Postgres, MySQL or the Google Visualization language. This package is the security boundary: no client-supplied query text is ever executed, every identifier is resolved against the source's stored schema, and SQL values are bound as parameters.
exposes: Spec{Table, Fields []Field, Filters []Filter, Sorts []Sort, Limit} — persisted as reports.query_spec JSONB
Compile(spec, datasource.Schema, Dialect, now time.Time) (Compiled, error)
Aggregate (none/sum/avg/min/max/count) + Aggregates slice; Operator set + Operators()
depends_on: datasource (Schema type only — no DB, no network)
key_notes: This package replaced LLM-generated SQL (commit 'Fixed sql injection vulnerability'). Any change here is security-relevant: aggregates come from the sqlFunction whitelist, operators from the operatorArities whitelist, identifiers from the schema, and SQL values only reach the text through bind().

Compile takes `now` as a parameter so a compile is reproducible and testable. Relative date operators (last_days, this_month, last_month) are expanded at compile time into fixed >= / < bounds in UTC — which is why a report's Spec is recompiled on every run rather than its stored SQL being reused.

Output column names are derived in resolve.go: outputName() gives `sum_amount` for an aggregate, the bare column name otherwise, and `row_count` for a bare count. Template slot mappings are stored against THESE names, so changing outputName breaks saved reports.
A sort must name one of the selected fields — ordering by an unselected column is rejected, not silently added to the select list.

Filter values are coerced to the column's type family (familyOf() matches on substrings of the source's own type name like 'int4', 'timestamptz') before compiling, so a bad value is a 400 rather than a database error.

Google Sheets has no parameter binding, so sheetsLiteral() writes values into the query text. It is deliberately strict: it picks whichever quote character the value does not contain, and REFUSES values containing both ' and " or any control character. Do not 'fix' this by adding escaping.

Sheets addresses columns by letter (A, B, ... AA) derived from the column's position in the stored header row — so a user inserting a spreadsheet column silently shifts every saved report until the schema is refreshed.
COUNT(*) is unsupported on Sheets (the gviz language has no count(*)); sheetsFieldExpression returns ErrInvalidSpec telling the user to count a specific column.
`contains` compiles to LIKE ... ESCAPE '!' on SQL (backslash avoided because engines disagree about it) and to CONTAINS on Sheets.
Adding a data source type requires an entry in the `dialects` map here plus a compile branch in Compile() — this is the only place query building learns about a source type.
